Overview

ComfortFirst HVAC is a fictional small HVAC company used as a real-world scenario to build and test a lead response automation system. The system captures customer service requests through a Google Form, stores them in Google Sheets, and automatically sends personalized emails to leads within seconds of submission. Urgent alerts go to the business owner at the same time.

The project was built in two versions: one using Make.com as a visual no-code automation tool, and a second using Google Apps Script for a fully free, native implementation inside Google Sheets.

Tech Stack

Google Forms Google Sheets Make.com Google Apps Script JavaScript Gmail

The Problem

Research shows the average business takes 47 hours to respond to a web lead. But responding within 5 minutes makes a business 21 times more likely to qualify that lead. For a small HVAC company, a missed emergency call in the summer heat isn't just a lost sale. It's a lost customer relationship.

The goal was to close that gap entirely: replace a slow, manual follow-up process with an automated system that responds instantly, every time, without relying on someone watching their inbox.

How It Works

Google Form → Google Sheets → Automation Engine → Gmail | (Routes by urgency level) / \ Auto-reply to Lead Owner Alert (emergencies only)

A customer submits a service request through a Google Form, selecting their service type and urgency level. That response lands in Google Sheets, which triggers the automation engine. Based on the urgency tier (Browsing, Warm, Hot, or Emergency), the system sends a personalized auto-reply to the customer and, for emergencies, a separate alert email to the business owner.

Urgency Tiers

Not every lead needs the same response. The system classifies each submission into one of four tiers so the right message goes out every time:

  • Browsing. General inquiry, friendly informational reply.
  • Warm. Specific service interest, reply with scheduling prompt.
  • Hot. Ready to book, reply with direct call to action.
  • Emergency. No heat or AC, reply with urgency and owner alert triggered.

Two Implementations

Make.com (Visual No-Code)

The first version uses Make.com's visual scenario builder with a Watch Rows trigger, a Router module, and Filter conditions for each urgency tier. It runs on a 15-minute polling cycle and handles roughly 250 to 330 leads per month on the free tier, enough for a small local business.

Google Apps Script (Native)

The second version runs entirely inside Google Sheets using a JavaScript-based Apps Script trigger. Because it fires on form submission rather than polling, the response goes out in seconds rather than minutes. There's no third-party account required, no operation limits, and the free tier supports 3,000+ leads per month, a meaningful step up for a growing business.

Email Templates

Each email is personalized with the lead's name, requested service, and a tone matched to their urgency level. Emergency replies lead with empathy and direct action steps. Browsing replies are warmer and informational. All emails include the company's contact details and a clear next step.

Reflection

This project was my first real automation build, and the biggest lesson was how much you can accomplish without writing a full application. Google Forms, Sheets, and Gmail already handle data capture, storage, and delivery. The automation layer just connects them intelligently.

Building the same workflow twice, once in Make.com and once in Apps Script, made the trade-offs concrete. Make.com is faster to set up and easier to visualize. Apps Script is faster to execute and free to scale. Knowing when to use each tool is its own skill.

Future plans include urgency-based email templates with different content per tier, SMS delivery via Twilio, and a 24-hour follow-up sequence for leads that don't respond to the initial reply.
